summary: Henrico County says the Upper Henrico tower was demolished in the late 1980s; a list places a standing tower at Gillies Creek that we could not confirm.

events.note: Henrico County page says two fire towers were built in Henrico County in the early 1930s, with parts assembled by the U.S. Forest Service; the Upper Henrico Tower appears to be the Short Pump tower
Mason Wade was the attendant of the Short Pump tower and went up it twice a day to watch for forest fires
Upper Henrico Tower demolished in the late 1980s, per Henrico County
Historical Society says a fire tower similar to its photograph was preserved in Goochland County; not confirmed as the Short Pump tower
Association lists the tower as relocated from Short Pump to Gillies Creek, under the heading Relocated / Replica Lookouts; no date or mover given

corrections.why: Only the association list says a tower stands at Gillies Creek. Henrico County says the Upper Henrico tower was demolished in the late 1980s, and the Historical Society places a similar tower in Goochland County. No page we read confirms a standing tower at Gillies Creek.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Historical Society calls its Goochland tower similar to the one in its photograph, not the Short Pump tower itself. Read that way, a Goochland tower need not contradict Henrico County's demolition account, but neither source names it as the Short Pump tower.

notes_for_editor: The Upper Henrico to Short Pump identification is inferred from name and place. The Gillies Creek standing claim rests on the association list alone, with no date or mover. A 2009 Waymarking post (WM6Q0E) says the Goochland exhibit tower may be the Short Pump tower or a Hanover tower and that the Short Pump tower's location is unknown; fetch_text cannot read that page because its content sits inside a form tag, so it is not cited and a human could check it by hand. A Facebook group post asks whether a Short Pump tower went to Gillies Creek; it is a question and was not read as evidence. The association list also has a Goochland entry named Field Day of the Past (Relocated Negrofoot) marked Tower Gone; the story does not use it because it names no Short Pump link. Consider a call to Henrico County. No photos found.
